the identification of a suitable cell source for bone tissue engineering and the development of a suitable isolation protocol for osteoprogenitor cells.
the isolation of subpopulations of periosteal cells, which have an enhanced osteogenic potential and could be used in future bone tissue engineering strategies.
a better understanding of human periosteal cells, which may be used in the future for bone tissue engineering and cell based regenerative medicine.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MSCA- 1 is a marker for a subpopulation of periosteal stem cells with a higher osteoprogenitor potential, which can be isolated by MACS separation.
MSCA- 1+ CPCs have a higher osteogenic differentiation potential than the MSCA- 11- CPCs.
MSCA- 1 is a more reliable marker for the isolation and characterization of osteoprogenitor cells from CPCs than CD146.

CD146 is not an osteoprogenitor marker.
MSCA- 1+ CPCs represent a valuable subpopulation for the generation of bone tissue engineered products.
